- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the following days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if price is deviating significantly from 30-day moving average, forecast should align closer to that average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ sentiment-weighted price.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model exhibits high variance; use median of recent 10-day forecast instead of mean to reduce noise.
